description: The Metal Tiger in Chinese astrology: personality, Metal element traits, 1950 and 2010 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Metal Tiger is the Tiger born in a Metal year, one of five versions of the third animal. It combines the Tiger's courage with Metal's qualities. Metal Tiger years between 1924 and 2044 are 1950 and 2010. The Tiger's fixed element is Wood.

sections.heading: The Metal Tiger personality
paragraphs: The Metal Tiger faces a direct challenge from its own year element. Metal controls Wood in the five-element cycle, and the Tiger's fixed element is Wood, so the stem is said to cut and discipline the Tiger's expansive nature, producing a sharper, more intense character. Metal Tigers are often described as determined, ambitious and fiercely independent, with strong convictions and little tolerance for obstacles. They tend to set high goals and pursue them relentlessly. The pressure of Metal on Wood gives them focus and resilience, yet it can also create inner strain, showing up as impatience, defensiveness or an all-or-nothing approach that leaves little room for compromise or rest. Few combinations are as hard to discourage.

Metal is the element of autumn and harvest, and a Metal year is traditionally said to sharpen whatever animal it meets. Descriptions associate it with determination, discipline, clear judgement and a strong code of principle. Metal-year people are often portrayed as decisive, self-reliant and willing to do difficult things because they are right. The element is linked with refinement and with cutting away what is unnecessary, so it tends to bring focus and high standards. Its traditional shadow is rigidity: Metal can become inflexible, proud or emotionally guarded, preferring to be correct over being close, and finding it hard to bend once a position is taken.

sections.heading: Metal Tiger at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Metal is usually linked with discipline, precision and principled leadership. Metal-year people are often described as the ones who set standards, cut through confusion and finish what they start, which suits law, engineering, finance, surgery, editing and any role that values exactness. They tend to work well alone and lead by example. The traditional caution is inflexibility: a Metal stem can dismiss ideas that arrive untidily, so practising curiosity before judgement usually makes them better leaders.

The Metal Tiger approaches a career like a duel: focused, competitive and determined to win cleanly. Law, competitive sport, security work, investigative journalism and turnaround management come up again and again, since each tests nerve and principle together. It performs best with a clearly defined target and minimal micromanagement, and colleagues usually admire its candour even while flinching at its bluntness. As a partner, the Metal Tiger is intensely loyal and defends the people it loves without a moment's hesitation. It wants an equal who will not be intimidated by its intensity. Conflict appears when certainty hardens into an all-or-nothing stance, turning a small disagreement about holidays or chores into a contest that somebody has to lose.

sections.heading: Metal Tiger years and dates
paragraphs: The table from 1924 to 2044 holds 2 Metal Tiger years: 1950, starting Feb 17 and 2010, starting Feb 14. Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1950 anyone born before Feb 17 is a Earth Ox, not a Metal Tiger. It takes sixty years for the Metal stem and the Tiger branch to coincide again, which is why the same pairing marks grandparents and grandchildren rather than siblings. Every Metal Tiger year is Yang, matching the Tiger's own polarity.

In the sexagenary calendar this is the Geng-Yin year, the Metal stem Geng with the Tiger's branch Yin. Births just before each new year fall in the Earth Ox year (before February 17, 1950) and the Earth Ox year (before February 14, 2010), and births in the weeks after each Metal Tiger year ends belong to the Metal Rabbit. The new year itself fell on a Friday in 1950 and Sunday in 2010.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Metal Tiger
paragraphs: For the Metal Tiger, growth usually means softening the blade. Readings often suggest that this combination benefits from deliberately seeking other perspectives before acting, since conviction can harden into tunnel vision. Metal Tigers may also be hard on themselves, treating setbacks as personal failures; self-compassion tends to make them more resilient, not less. Activities that bring calm, such as swimming, music or long walks, help release tension. Because they fight fiercely for what they believe, choosing battles carefully saves energy. When the Metal Tiger channels its intensity wisely, it becomes a principled and effective champion of its causes.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Metal Tiger shares the Tiger's San He trine with the Horse and Dog (the Fire trine), its Liu He bond with the Pig, and its Liu Chong clash with the Monkey. The element adds a second layer: another Metal sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Metal in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Metal Tiger years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1950 (from February 17, 1950) and 2010 (from February 14, 2010). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Metal Tiger's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Metal and the Tiger's fixed element is Wood; in the five-element cycles metal controls Wood. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Metal Tiger?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Horse and Dog (San He) and the Pig (Liu He). The Monkey is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Metal Tiger called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Geng-Yin. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Metal stem Geng, followed by its earthly branch, here Yin for the Tiger, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Metal Tiger different from other Tigers?
faq.answer: All Tigers share courage, independence and magnetic energy. The Metal year element changes the tone: metal is the element of autumn and harvest, and a Metal year is traditionally said to sharpen whatever animal it meets.
